doc.title: Longineu Parsons interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 17, 2026

title: Nat Adderley's horn and meeting the Adderleys at Florida A&M
summary: Parsons plays Nat Adderley's horn; Nat and Cannonball knew his father at Florida A&M, and Parsons impressed them at a student seminar where Nat promised to look out for him.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Cannonball Adderley: the sound, the man, the band

blocks.x: The other name I wanted to bring up, and I know it’s dear to both of us, is the Adderleys.

That’s what I say, oh. I just felt that Cannonball, for me, was it. He just exuded everything I wanted to be like a saxophone player, a spokesman, and then I got into their music, especially in the sixties, and eventually I was able to sit with Nat Adderley for an hour and it was a highlight of my life.
Are you going to tell me that that’s Nat Adderley’s horn?
That’s right. This is the one he did those recordings with Cannonball on.
Oh how did you end up with that?
The family wanted me to play it.

Nat raised me as a musician. He and Cannonball knew my father when they were all here at Florida A&M as students. And see ‘cause when I started playing the horn, see my parents always had music in the house growing up. And my dad said, “Oh you’re playing the cornet, well you’ve got to hear Nat Adderley, that’s my buddy from school you know, and Cannonball Adderley and them. And so, and they were all part of the same social circles, you know all the doctor this and professor this and this and that and the other. You know so it was, “Yeah, if you’re going to play music, you listen to them.” And they played Duke Ellington for me all the time, well they played all the time, listening to Duke Ellington and Lionel Hampton and my mother liked Dinah Washington and Ella Fitzgerald and Sarah Vaughan and yeah, the Adderleys. And then what happened was when I came back to school to be a musician I was – well Cannonball and Nat would come in to do a concert at Florida A&M. And so I knew, I was waiting for them to come up, they were going to do like a little seminar during the day, before the concert. And so I knew they’d be coming up, so I could see them drive up so I could meet them, and I came up and said, “Oh, I know who you are” and all that. Because I’m junior, so I said “My name is Longineu.” “Oh yeah, oh okay yeah, uh huh. How’s your dad doing?” Yeah it was like that. And then Cannonball and Nat were speaking to us, the students in the recital hall and they played something. He had Hal Galper on piano and Roy McCurdy on drums. And a guy sitting next to me, another trumpet player in the band whose last name was McCurdy, he said, “I wonder if I’m related to him.” Turned out they are cousins. And so then Cannonball played something, Cannonball and Nat, and then they opened it up and said, “Okay well let’s see, hear the students play.” And they were surprised that we had a line of students who could really improvise but I went first. I pushed – I made sure I could play first. And I started playing and they were in the back doing like Cannonball and Nat would do, I’m sure it was something illegal, not to be talked about. And then I’m playing and then what I heard was, after I started playing Nat and Cannonball came back out to look to see what was going on, to see who is this playing. And Nat said, “Look you stick close to me” you know, “I’ll look out for you.” And he called my mother and told her the same thing and said, “Look, you don’t let him sign any contract without talking to me.”
